review.reason: Read theorem assumptions, proof overview, and permutation large-deviation argument. Connects probability, optimization, and matrix spectra.

item.title: Free probability via entropic optimal transport
item.headline: A new bridge between random matrices and ordinary probability
item.authors: Octavio Arizmendi and Samuel G. G. Johnston
item.summary: A proof expresses free-probability operations through optimization over ordinary random variables. Its matrix interpretation concerns limiting eigenvalue distributions, not exact finite matrices.

evidence.question: Can ordinary probability describe how large random matrices combine?
evidence.method: Mathematical proof combining characteristic-polynomial identities with large-deviation theory.
evidence.limitations: The formulas assume compactly supported distributions and specified parameter ranges.

explainer.finding: The optimization balances a logarithmic reward against an entropy penalty for dependence between paired variables.
explainer.method: The proof weighs unusually favorable permutations against their rarity.
explainer.meaning: For example, it offers another description of the limiting eigenvalue distribution when two independent, unitarily invariant Hermitian random matrices are added.
explainer.limits: This theoretical connection does not establish a faster practical algorithm.
